name: Match Between System and the Real World
description: Interfaces should present concepts, language, and ordering in terms users already understand rather than internal system logic. The goal is not literal skeuomorphism but conceptual fit with the user's world.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to naming, information architecture, empty states, data labels, icons/metaphors, and workflow sequencing that matches how users think about the task.
myth_risk_note: No peer-reviewed finding validates 'match between system and real world' as a discrete design principle with empirical support. The heuristic is intuitively reasonable and supported by HCI practice wisdom, but lacks experimental evidence comparable to principles like selective attention or perceptual grouping. Consistent with this entry's existing no_rigorous_backing_found status.
prevalence_note: Part of Nielsen's canonical top ten and still standard review language in UX, product writing, and design-system critique.

applications.title: Cars.com's unrecognizable skeuomorphic photo-gallery scroll controls
applications.description: NN/g's own usability review observed gray half-circle controls with white symbols in the lower corners of Cars.com's photo-gallery images, intended to let users scroll left/right through the gallery. The controls loosely resembled the folded corners of a photo in a physical scrapbook, but didn't read as buttons or arrows and didn't match any familiar real-world or digital paging metaphor -- cited as a failed attempt at skeuomorphic design that broke the 'match between system and the real world' heuristic instead of reinforcing it.
applications.ethical_note: A pure usability failure with no persuasion or manipulation angle -- the cost here runs against the business and the user alike (users can't find the scroll controls, the site gains nothing from the confusion). Included as a concrete, named, current-format illustration of what happens when a design breaks this heuristic rather than following it, alongside the corpus's existing positive examples of the heuristic being followed correctly.
